sections.title: What you know
sections.content: From the first lesson of this unit you know the basic contrast: *Busco un apartamento que tenga balcón* for a flat you have not found, and *Tengo un apartamento que tiene balcón* for a real one. This lesson adds two things: a small clue in the word before the noun, and the same contrast in the past.

sections.title: Same frame, two meanings
rows: Busco a la chica que habla inglés.
I'm looking for the girl who speaks English (I know who she is).
Busco una chica que hable inglés.
I'm looking for a girl who speaks English (any girl).
Necesitaba un cargador que sirviera para mi móvil.
I needed a charger that would work for my phone (I didn't know if there was one).
Encontré un cargador que servía para mi móvil.
I found a charger that worked for my phone (a real one).

sections.title: The article, and the past
sections.content: First, the word before the noun is a clue. *El*, *la*, *los* and *las* usually point at something known, so the indicative follows. *Un* and *una* often go with something open, so the subjunctive follows. It is only a clue: *Conozco a una chica que habla inglés* has *una* and is still a real person. Second, in the past the subjunctive moves to the imperfect subjunctive. You know the *-ra* forms from B1 Unit 4: *Necesitaba un cargador que sirviera*. Once you have found the thing, the indicative returns: *Encontré uno que servía*.

items.english: I need a charger that works (any that works).
I have a charger that works (this one).

items.spanish: Busco la tienda que está cerca de la oficina.
items.english: I'm looking for the shop that is near the office (I know which one).

items.spanish: Busco una tienda que esté cerca de la oficina.
items.english: I'm looking for a shop that is near the office (any shop).

sections.content: When English gives you no clue, trust the meaning: do I know which one it is? If yes, indicative. If any one will do, or I do not know whether it exists, subjunctive. In the past, the same two choices become imperfect subjunctive (*sirviera*) and imperfect indicative (*servía*).
